title: Majesty that a mountain could not bear to see
subtitle: Al-Jalil: the Majestic, whose perfection fills the heart with awe and love
intro: Al-Jalil (الْجَلِيلُ) means The Majestic: the One described with every attribute of greatness, might and perfection, so exalted that He deserves awe and reverence for who He is. His majesty is not cold; it is joined to generosity. Knowing this name gives your faith its proper seriousness and your love its proper depth.

root.sense: Jalla means to be great, lofty and imposing. Jalal is majesty: the quality of someone so honored and impressive that you lower your gaze in their presence, the reason people say Your Majesty. Applied to Allah, it is the sum of His perfect attributes of greatness, seen together, inspiring awe.

picture.label: Two sides the Quran holds together

row.title: God is just my easygoing friend

knowing: Al-Jalil is the One who possesses every attribute of majesty in full: power, greatness, knowledge, honor, independence, holiness. {idea}Al-Ghazali explained the near names this way: Al-Kabir points to the perfection of His essence, Al-Jalil to the perfection of His attributes, and Al-Azim to both together as they overwhelm the mind{/idea}. Al-Jalil is majesty you feel when you contemplate who He is.

This exact form is not used as a name in the Quran; it comes in the well-known lists of the names reported in the hadith collections. Its meaning, though, runs through the Quran in the phrase Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram, Owner of Majesty and Generosity (55:27, 55:78). That pairing matters. {reward}His majesty never makes Him harsh, and His generosity never makes Him small.{/reward}

Many speak of God only as love, and forget majesty. Others speak only of His might, and forget mercy. Al-Jalil restores the balance. Too much fear without hope leads to despair; too much hope without awe leads to carelessness. The believer flies with both wings.
seeing: Musa asked to see his Lord. He was told to look at the mountain: if it stayed in place, he would see Him. When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, it crumbled to dust, and Musa fell unconscious (7:143). That is a glimpse of jalal: a majesty that solid rock could not withstand.

Surah ar-Rahman turns on the same idea. After describing the gifts of creation, it says everyone on earth will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Generosity (55:26-27). Everything we admire fades; His majesty remains.

And in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ said that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will ask: where are those who loved one another for the sake of My majesty? Today I will shade them in My shade, on a day when there is no shade but Mine.
trusting: Awe is not the enemy of trust; it is its foundation. You hand your affairs only to someone you take seriously. {idea}Because He is Al-Jalil, His promises are weighty, His care is not casual, and His decisions are never small{/idea}. When you stand in prayer feeling His majesty, the things that terrify you outside lose their grip.

His majesty is also why He forgives so fully. A petty ruler holds grudges; a majestic one can afford to pardon. {reward}Approach Al-Jalil with your sins and your needs, reverent and hopeful, and you are approaching the most generous Majesty there is.{/reward}
loving: Love without respect grows shallow, and respect without love grows cold. In Al-Jalil the heart finds both. {reward}Love for His sake is so precious to Him that He promised His shade to those who loved one another for His majesty.{/reward} Loving Him and loving people for His sake is how we answer His majesty.
now: You catch yourself scrolling while the imam recites, half-praying out of habit. {idea}Pause and picture the mountain that crumbled before His majesty, then remember that same Lord is listening to you now.{/idea} Lower your gaze, slow your recitation, and feel the honor of standing before Al-Jalil.
old: I treat Allah casually, like a background presence in my day.
new: Al-Jalil is majestic beyond measure and generous beyond measure, and standing before Him is an honor.
try: Repeat Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram a few times in your dua today, and pause to feel both halves of it: majesty and generosity.

dua.text: Ya Jalil, Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram, fill my heart with awe of Your majesty and hope in Your generosity. Shade me with those who love one another for Your sake, and let nothing in this world outweigh You in my heart.
dua.note: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged persisting with Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram in supplication, as reported by at-Tirmidhi; it is a natural way to call on Al-Jalil.

pairs.why: Al-Jalil is His majesty; Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram shows that majesty always comes joined with generosity and honor.
Majesty that inspires awe, generosity that inspires hope: together they keep the heart between fear and love.
Al-Kabir points to the perfection of His essence, Al-Jalil to the perfection of His attributes.

faq.a: Al-Jalil means The Majestic. It describes Allah as the One who possesses every attribute of greatness and perfection in full, so exalted that He deserves awe and reverence for who He is. His majesty is always joined with generosity.

faq.q: Is Al-Jalil mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: The exact name Al-Jalil is not used in the Quran; it appears in the well-known lists of the 99 names transmitted in the hadith collections. Its meaning is in the Quranic phrase Dhul-Jalali wal-Ikram, Owner of Majesty and Generosity, in 55:27 and 55:78.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Jalil, Al-Kabir and Al-Azim?
faq.a: Al-Ghazali explained that Al-Kabir refers to the perfection of Allah's essence, Al-Jalil to the perfection of His attributes, and Al-Azim to both together, overwhelming the mind's ability to grasp them. All three describe greatness from a different angle.

faq.q: What does Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram mean?
faq.a: It means O Owner of Majesty and Generosity. It calls on Allah by both His awe-inspiring greatness and His kindness. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged persisting with it in dua, as reported by at-Tirmidhi.
